stem: My mom puts the ____ on to keep her hands away from water when she washes the dishes.
explain_zh: 洗碗前為了不讓水碰到手，會戴上gloves(手套)。jacket是外套、ring是戒指、socks是襪子，都與防水無關。put on gloves是常見固定搭配，看到「保護雙手接觸水」就該聯想到手套。

stem: Can you ____ your feet a little off the floor? I want to see if my keys are under the sofa.
explain_zh: 把腳稍微抬離地面，好讓人看沙發底下，用raise(舉起、抬起)最合語意。check是檢查、kick是踢、show是給人看，語意都不符合「抬離地面」的動作。raise是常考的及物動詞，後面直接加受詞。

stem: ____ of my sisters are older than I am. I'm the youngest of the three children in my family.
explain_zh: 說話者是三個小孩中最小的，代表另外兩個姊姊都比自己年長，剛好是「兩者」，須用Both(兩者都)。Most、Few、Some通常用來描述三者以上的範圍，用在「只有兩個」的情境並不精確。看到「只有兩者」就該直接想到Both。

stem: The beach near our town is a very ____ place. Every summer at least one kid dies there in the water.
explain_zh: 後句提到每年都有小孩在該處溺斃，可知這是形容海灘dangerous(危險的)。exciting(刺激的)、lonely(孤單的)、popular(受歡迎的)都無法呼應「溺水身亡」的描述。看到跟死亡、風險有關的敘述，就該聯想到dangerous。

stem: My wife enjoys going to the movies with her friends, but I like to watch TV at home by ____.
explain_zh: by oneself是固定片語，表示「獨自一人」，主詞是I，反身代名詞須對應為myself。I是主格、me是受格、mine是所有格代名詞，文法上都不能放在by之後表達「獨自」的意思。by myself、by yourself等要背熟，是常考的反身代名詞句型。

stem: For the past twenty years, my father ____ in a school library. But he'll leave the job next month.
explain_zh: for the past twenty years表示「過去二十年直到現在」，動作持續到現在，須用現在完成式has worked。worked是簡單過去式(動作已結束)、is working是現在進行式、works是簡單現在式，都無法表達「從過去持續至今」的語意。看到for+一段時間，且動作還沒結束，就要想到現在完成式。

vocab.w: for the past + 一段時間

stem: It's great that we can buy train tickets over the phone without going out. It ____ us a lot of time.
explain_zh: 用電話訂票不用出門，可以幫忙「省下」時間，因此用saves(節省)最合語意。lends是借出、prepares是準備、takes是花費，語意都不符合「不用出門」帶來的好處。save + 人 + 時間/金錢是常見句型，意思是「幫某人省下…」。

stem: Mozart ____ his first music when he was only six years old.
explain_zh: when he was only six years old是明確的過去時間點，須用簡單過去式wrote。is writing是現在進行式、has written是現在完成式、will write是未來式，時態都與「六歲時」這個已結束的過去時間點不符。明確的過去時間點是簡單過去式最重要的判斷線索。

stem: Jill: Have you decided ____ you will celebrate your 30th birthday? Sue: Yeah, I'm going to have a big barbecue party.
explain_zh: Sue的回答是「辦一個烤肉派對」，說明的是慶祝的方式，因此問句要用how(如何)。where問地點、what問內容、when問時間，都對不上回答中「用什麼方式慶祝」的內容。要根據回答的內容，反推前面該用哪個疑問詞。

stem: Alison doesn't like ____ what to do. She only does things she wants to do.
explain_zh: Alison不喜歡「被告知」該做什麼，是不定詞的被動式，須用to be told。told是過去分詞單獨使用不合文法、to tell是主動不定詞、be told缺少to，都不符合like之後接不定詞的規則。不定詞的被動式格式是to be + p.p.，常與like、want等動詞搭配使用。

stem: Josh has planned to make a trip to New York and ____ some of his friends there.
explain_zh: and連接兩個並列的不定詞片語，plan to make a trip and (to) visit，第二個to可省略，動詞須用原形visit。visits、visiting、visited都不符合省略to後應接原形動詞的文法規則。並列結構中重複出現的to常可省略，是常考的文法重點。

stem: Ms. Johnson has been taking phone calls since she entered the office this morning. Just when she thought she could finally leave work, ____ call came in.
explain_zh: 電話一通接一通，還會有更多通不確定是哪一通的電話，用another(不特定的再一通)最合語意。each指「每一個」、the next指「下一個」(過於特定)、the other指「兩者中的另一個」，都不符合「還有其他不特定來電」的情境。another強調「同類但不特定的另一個」，是常考的限定詞辨析。

stem: We were so sure that Jerry ____ well on the difficult job. His past experience in other work showed he was the right guy for it. So when he failed, no one believed it.
explain_zh: 站在過去的時間點，對未來(Jerry會不會做得好)所做的預測，須用過去未來式would do。had done是過去完成式、did是簡單過去式、has done是現在完成式，都無法表達「過去對未來的預測」。過去未來式常用在「過去覺得將來會怎樣」的描述中，要與過去完成式仔細區分。

stem: For Mike, the price is ____ important thing when he shops for jeans. He cares even more about the shape and the size of the pockets.
explain_zh: 後半句說Mike更在意口袋的形狀和大小，代表價格反而是他最不在意的事，須用the least(最不)表達最高程度的「不重要」。the more/the most都是「較多／最多」，語意相反；the less雖也表「較少」，但此句需要最高級程度，須用the least。看到even more的對比語氣，就能判斷第一件事是「最不重要」。

stem: What is it in the reading?
explain_zh: 詩中描述衣物在曬衣繩上飄動、樹木花朵搖擺、雲朵彷彿在賽跑，都是風吹拂萬物的畫面，因此答案是wind。sun(太陽)、rain(雨)、rainbow(彩虹)都無法讓衣物飄動或使樹葉四處飛散。抓住「吹動」「搖擺」等動作性描述，就能聯想到風的意象。
passage:

Everyone cheers.
The shirts and shorts dance
On the clothesline,
The trees and flowers wave
Like they're saying hi,
And the clouds are so excited
To have a running race.

When it comes,
Dad's face falls.
His coat and jeans jump
Off the clothesline
Into the pond.
The tree leaves hop off
And have a party on his new car.

When it gets here,
A lot of fun things I notice:
The pond's face,
Sad and old with lines;
Mrs. Smith's bread,
Delicious and freshly baked.

Oh, no, it's from Mr. Brown's feet!

stem: How does Dad feel "when it comes"?
explain_zh: 第二段描述外套被吹落水塘、新車蓋滿落葉，「Dad's face falls」(臉垮下來)表示他看到這些狀況並不開心，符合選項C。scared是害怕、excited是興奮、interested是感興趣，都與「臉垮下來」的反應不符。face falls是常見的情緒描寫片語，表示失望、不悅。

stem: What can we learn about Buffy's friends?
options: Matt has experience of yard sales.
Jamie had a successful yard sale last week.
Albert thinks weather is important for yard sales.
Debby thinks things are cheaper online than at yard sales.
explain_zh: Matt在對話最後說他在上次的庭院拍賣交到好朋友，顯示他之前辦過或參加過庭院拍賣，符合選項A。Jamie上週其實是把東西送人，並沒有辦拍賣；Debby認為辦拍賣費工又賺得少，並未提到「線上比較便宜」；Albert提到「挑對日子」，但沒有特別強調天氣。要仔細對應每位角色說話的內容，才能正確配對選項。
passage:
Buffy: Hey, guys! I have a lot of things I don't need, so I'm thinking about having a yard sale. What do you think?
Debby: Having a yard sale is not easy. You have to collect things, put prices on them, put them out on tables and then wait for people to come. And usually you have to sell things at VERY low prices. For all that time and work, you make very little money. Why not just sell your things online for higher prices?
Jamie: Debby's right. But I think it'd be even better to just give your things to people who need them. I just sent out a lot of things last week.
Albert: Hey, I love yard sales! It's a great chance to make big money if you pick the right day. In my experience, Saturday is the best.
Matt: I agree with Albert. You can make money and meet interesting people. I made some good friends at my last yard sale.

stem: What do Buffy's friends think about having a yard sale?
options: Albert and Matt think it's a nice way to make friends.
Debby and Albert think it's difficult to make money from it.
Matt agrees with Jamie that it's a good chance to help people.
Jamie agrees with Debby that it's a lot of trouble to prepare for it.
explain_zh: Jamie回覆Debby時說「Debby's right」，直接認同Debby先前提到「辦拍賣很費工夫、賺不了多少錢」的看法，符合選項D。Albert和Matt其實很喜歡辦拍賣，也提到能交到朋友，並非覺得難以做到；Matt認同的是Albert的看法，不是Jamie的「送人」提議。閱讀對話時要留意「right」「agree」這類表示認同的用詞，才能正確配對是誰同意誰。

stem: From the ad, which is true about Sunny Sun pictures?
options: The first day to use Sunny Sun pictures is Feb. 4.
The last day to collect Sunny Sun pictures is Feb. 10.
You cannot use Sunny Sun pictures to get free desserts.
You cannot get Sunny Sun pictures when you buy books.
explain_zh: 廣告明確寫出消費金額須「except books and CDs」才能累積Sunny Sun貼紙，代表買書無法得到貼紙，符合選項D。廣告寫的是使用期限到2/10、而非蒐集期限到2/4，且明確可以用貼紙換取甜點，因此A、B、C皆與廣告內容不符。閱讀廣告題要特別留意EXCEPT等排除語，避免弄混使用期與蒐集期。
passage:
From Jan. 4 to Feb. 4, for each $50 you spend (on anything EXCEPT books and CDs) at Sunny Market, you'll get a Sunny Sun picture. (2 pictures for every $100, 3 pictures for every $150, …)
Collect 12 pictures, and you can get a Sunny Cup for free!
Collect 10 pictures, and you can get any of the desserts on the right for free!
Collect 6 pictures, and you can buy a Sunny Cup for $200, or any of the desserts on the right for $100!
From Jan. 4 to Feb. 10, you can use Sunny Sun pictures to get Sunny Cups or desserts.
With Sunny Sun pictures, you can get one of the prizes below for free or at low prices!! Sunny Cup, Chocolate, Fruitcake, Ice cream

stem: Sammy has 7 Sunny Sun pictures. She wants to get a Sunny Cup. How can she get one?
options: Use 6 Sunny Sun pictures and pay $100.
Use 6 Sunny Sun pictures and pay $200.
Spend $150 to get 3 more Sunny Sun pictures.
Spend $200 to get 4 more Sunny Sun pictures.
explain_zh: 廣告寫明集滿6張貼紙可用$200購買Sunny Cup，Sammy手上已有7張，只要用其中6張並付$200即可，符合選項B。她不需要再花$150或$200去多換貼紙，也不是用6張只付$100(那是換免費甜點的門檻，不是Sunny Cup的價格)。這類題要對照廣告上不同集點門檻分別對應的優惠內容，不要混淆。

stem: What does "them" mean in the reading?
explain_zh: 前一句提到製作巧克力甜點常需混合奶油與糖，「if you do」指的就是「如果你要混合」，因此them指的是butter and sugar，符合選項B。Bains-marie是隔水加熱法的名稱、chocolate desserts是甜點成品，都與這句要放入鍋中的對象不同；small pieces of chocolate雖也在前一句出現，但主詞位置離them較遠。找代名詞指涉時要往「最靠近、語意最貼切」的名詞去找。
passage:
Now I'm going to show you how to work with chocolate. I'll do it in a "bain-marie," or, well, some people call it "water bath." I myself love the name "bain-marie." To make a "bain-marie," you need two pots, one bigger than the other.
First, break the chocolate into small pieces and put them in the smaller pot. Usually when making chocolate desserts, you'll need to mix chocolate with butter and sugar. So if you do, put them in the pot too.
Now, half fill the bigger pot with warm water. Put the smaller pot over the bigger one, and start to slowly mix the chocolate, the butter, and the sugar together. Keep the water under 50ºC, or the chocolate may lose its shine. And make sure that no water goes in the smaller pot, or the chocolate will become hard and cannot be used.
Keep mixing for about five to ten minutes, and the job is done. Easy, right?

stem: From the reading, which is true about working with chocolate?
options: It is better to use a "bain-marie" than a "water bath."
The water in the pot should not be warmer than 50ºC.
It is better to finish mixing it in less than five minutes.
We should not mix butter and sugar together at the same time.
explain_zh: 文中提醒要讓水維持在50ºC以下，否則巧克力會失去光澤，符合選項B。文章並未說bain-marie一定比water bath好(其實是同一種方法的兩種說法)，也沒有說攪拌時間要少於五分鐘，反而說要攪拌五到十分鐘；文中也沒說奶油和糖不能同時加入。細節題要逐句核對文中出現的數字與條件是否一致。

First, break the chocolate into small pieces and put them in the smaller pot. Usually when making chocolate desserts, you'll need to mix chocolate with butter and sugar. So if you do, put them in the pot too.

stem: What does the news story say about the Yangs' food truck?
options: What people love about their food.
What made them start their business.
How they made delicious fried chicken.
How they fixed their business problems.
explain_zh: 整篇新聞從生意冷清講到後來想出改名、換色、吸引顧客等方法讓生意變好，主軸是描述他們如何解決生意上的困境，符合選項D。文章雖提到菜單和創業年份，但重點並非「大家喜歡什麼食物」或「怎麼做出美味炸雞」，創業原因也只是背景交代而非主旨。掌握文章「slack→better」的前後轉折，能幫助抓住文章主旨。
passage:
During lunch time, on 53rd Street, you'll see a long line of people in front of a Taiwanese food truck for their "bian-dang," a Taiwanese word for "lunch box." On the menu you can find fried chicken with rice, pork dumplings, tea eggs, and other popular Taiwanese dishes.
The owners of the food truck are Thomas and Diana Yang, two Taiwanese-Americans. This brother-sister team started their business in 2009. Back then, there were a few Taiwanese restaurants in the city and several thousand food trucks, but the Yangs were the first to sell Taiwanese food on a food truck.
At first, business was slack. People thought they were just another Chinese food truck, and the food truck's name, "Cravings," often made people think of desserts, not lunch. Few people would stop by and try their food. "I couldn't even give away free food," said Thomas. To catch people's eye, they painted their truck blue, and drew Taiwan's national flower, the plum blossom, on it. They also changed the food truck's name to "bian-dang." Soon people started to notice them, and business finally got better. Now on a good day, they can sell about 150 bian-dangs in about two hours.
So what's next for Thomas and Diana? Well, they hope one day there will be a block with Taiwanese food in the city, just like there is a Chinatown, a Korea Town, and a Little Italy. And their bian-dang food truck might just help to make that happen.

stem: What does it mean when business is slack?
explain_zh: 後文描述「幾乎沒人上門、送都送不出去」，可知slack是形容生意「差」，符合選項A。business is slack不是指要出售(for sale)，也不是指生意興隆(growing)，更不是指每天營業(open every day)。slack常用來形容「(生意)清淡、蕭條」，可搭配上下文的負面描述判斷字義。

stem: What does "that" mean in the news story?
options: A city block that sells Taiwanese food.
A business that is popular across the country.
explain_zh: 前一句提到他們希望有一天城裡能出現像中國城一樣、專賣台灣美食的街區(a block with Taiwanese food)，而「their food truck might help make that happen」中的that就是指這個街區願景，符合選項C。並非指單一間台灣餐廳、第二台餐車，或全國知名的生意，這些都與前一句描述的「一整個街區」不同。指代題要找前一句語意最完整對應的名詞片語。

stem: What problem is Selena Bieber trying to fix?
options: High school lessons are too difficult.
Classes start too early in the morning.
Too many students are late for school.
Lunch break is too short for taking a rest.
explain_zh: 全信主題都在說明早上上課太早，讓學生睡不飽、無法專心，並呼籲學校延後上課時間，符合選項B。信中沒有提到課程太難、學生遲到或午休太短的問題，這些都不是作者要解決的重點。掌握信件最後的訴求「why can't school start later」最能看出寫信目的。
passage:
Do you feel it's hard to get up early for school and even harder to listen well in the first class at 8 a.m.? Well, this happens to most of us and is not helpful for our learning!
Some studies show that teenagers' brains make melatonin, the hormone that helps sleep, between 11 p.m. and 8 a.m. So it's better for us to sleep during these nine hours. But here comes the problem. We're asked to get to school by 7:30 a.m. That means we have to get up before 7, when our brains should still be sleeping. That's why we're always so tired and can't think clearly in early morning classes. No clear head, no good learning, right?
If we can't change how our body works, why can't school start later? In this way, we can not only sleep more but also learn better!
Want to help us make it happen? Visit www.nvhsstudsup.org/later-better to learn more.

Below is some information from another study.
We studied 48 high school students and found that the students who went to bed earlier did better on their school tests. This is not only true for those who slept nine hours, but also true for those who slept less. And some of them agreed that they learned better in early morning classes.

stem: What can we learn from the letter?
options: Too much melatonin can hurt teenagers' brains.
The brain stops making melatonin after 11 p.m.
Sleeping longer helps the body make more melatonin.
It is easier to fall asleep when the brain is making melatonin.
explain_zh: 文中提到褪黑激素在晚上11點到早上8點之間分泌，能幫助入睡，代表分泌期間比較容易入睡，符合選項D。信中沒有說褪黑激素過多會傷腦(A)，也沒說11點後大腦就停止分泌(B，其實11點才剛開始分泌)；C選項則把「睡久一點」和「分泌更多褪黑激素」的因果關係說反了。讀懂melatonin與sleep之間的因果關係是解題關鍵。
passage:
Do you feel it's hard to get up early for school and even harder to listen well in the first class at 8 a.m.? Well, this happens to most of us and is not helpful for our learning!
Some studies show that teenagers' brains make melatonin, the hormone that helps sleep, between 11 p.m. and 8 a.m. So it's better for us to sleep during these nine hours. But here comes the problem. We're asked to get to school by 7:30 a.m. That means we have to get up before 7, when our brains should still be sleeping. That's why we're always so tired and can't think clearly in early morning classes. No clear head, no good learning, right?
If we can't change how our body works, why can't school start later? In this way, we can not only sleep more but also learn better!
Want to help us make it happen? Visit www.nvhsstudsup.org/later-better to learn more.

Below is some information from another study.
We studied 48 high school students and found that the students who went to bed earlier did better on their school tests. This is not only true for those who slept nine hours, but also true for those who slept less. And some of them agreed that they learned better in early morning classes.

stem: Below is some information from another study. Do the ideas in Selena Bieber's letter agree with the information?
options: Yes, because her letter says it is better to sleep from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m.
Yes, because her letter says getting up early is not helpful for learning.
No, because her letter says students are asked to get to school by 7:30 a.m.
No, because her letter says teenagers' brains do not work well in early morning classes.
explain_zh: 額外研究發現早睡的學生考試表現較好、有些人也認為早上上課學得更好，這與信中「早上腦袋不清楚、無法好好學習」的說法互相矛盾，因此答案是D(不同意，因為信中說青少年早上腦袋不清楚)。兩者的分歧點在於對「早晨學習效果」看法不同，而不是上學時間的規定本身，所以A、B、C都不夠精確。比對兩篇短文的立場差異是這類題型的核心技巧。

stem: What can we learn about Kivalina?
options: It is fighting for one last hope.
It has given up its chance to rise.
explain_zh: 文中提到居民仍在祈禱海水不要太快淹沒家園，也有ReLocate等團體努力協助搬遷，顯示他們仍在爭取最後一絲希望，符合選項C。文章並未說Kivalina已成為歷史(它現況危急但還沒消失)，也沒說居民已經放棄(D)或正等著發光發熱(A)。要抓住文末「still fighting、still praying」的語氣，判斷居民尚未放棄的心境。
passage:
Kivalina, an island village in Alaska, USA, is known by only a few people. It cannot be found on most maps of Alaska because it is only 10 km2. This small Arctic village is home to 400 Inuit people*. However, their home will become uninhabitable because the island could be covered by the Chukchi Sea by 2025. These Inuit people will have to leave their home.
But life now is already difficult. Over the past twenty years, winters have become warmer, the Arctic ice has kept melting, and the sea has been rising. These changes have made it harder to live by hunting and fishing than before. What's worse, there is no Arctic ice thick enough to keep them safe from terrible wind and rain.
These Inuit people think it is the oil and power companies in Alaska that have brought all these troubles, but they are the ones who are paying the price. It would cost hundreds of millions to move their village, and they have no idea where to get the money. Groups like ReLocate are working together with the Inuit people to save Kivalina, but nobody is sure if their hard work will come to anything. All the Inuit people can do now is to pray the rising sea will not cover their home too soon.
* The Inuit people are a group of people who live in the Arctic.

stem: What does it mean when we say a place is uninhabitable?
explain_zh: 後文說村莊即將被海水淹沒、居民勢必得搬走，因此uninhabitable指「無法居住」，符合選項D。uninhabitable與地方大小(A)、受不受歡迎(B)、能不能被買賣(C)都無關，純粹描述「不適合人居住」的狀態。字首un-加上habit(居住)、able(可以)，可以幫助猜出字義。

options: Their way of living has been hurting the earth.
They might not be able to get enough money to move their village.
They should make the oil and power companies fix their problems.

explain_zh: 文中提到搬遷需要數億元經費，而居民完全不知道錢從哪裡來，顯示作者擔心他們籌不到足夠的搬遷費用，符合選項B。文章並未指責Inuit人破壞環境(A)，也沒說該由石油公司出面解決(C)，更沒有提出比搬遷更好的方法(D)。留意「no idea where to get the money」這句話直接點出作者的隱憂。

options: The Arctic ice covered 10 km2 of Kivalina.
The melting Arctic ice kills about 400 Inuit people each year.
The Arctic ice helped the Inuit people in Kivalina during bad weather.
The melting Arctic ice has given the Inuit people enough water to use.
explain_zh: 文中提到現在沒有足夠厚的浮冰保護居民免受強風暴雨侵襲，暗示過去冰層原本能提供保護，符合選項C。文章沒有說冰層覆蓋整個10平方公里的Kivalina(A)，也沒提到冰融化每年直接害死400名居民(B)，或提供足夠飲用水(D)，這些都是過度延伸的說法。抓住「no longer thick enough to keep them safe」的對比語氣即可判斷。

stem: But before you decide whether it's OK to have such a long commute, it's best to know ____.
options: how you can enjoy it more
how it will change your life
what is the best way of commute for you
explain_zh: 文章接下來的段落描述長時間通勤會減少睡眠、影響健康與人際關係，都是在說明「通勤如何改變生活」，符合選項C。文中並未列出「還能做什麼其他事」(A)、「如何更享受通勤」(B)，也沒有提供「最佳通勤方式」的建議(D)，這些選項都偏離了後續段落的內容。先讀完整段落再回頭選空格答案，是克漏字常見的解題技巧。
passage:
After a lot of tests and interviews, you finally got into a good school or got a good job. But there's a problem: it's a long way from home. "Well, I can take the bus or drive," you might think. But before you decide whether it's OK to have such a long commute, it's best to know ____.
Having a long commute means you'll get fewer hours of sleep, and that'll make you feel tired easily. You'll also have less time for friends and family, for exercise, or for a nice meal.
A long commute not only eats up your time but also ____. Studies show that people who have a long commute get fat easily and often have neck or back problems. It's easier for them to have heart problems too. ____. Studies find that these people get angry more often, feel less happy with their lives, and do less well at work.
Now, does that good school or that good job still sound good to you?

stem: A long commute not only eats up your time but also ____.
explain_zh: 下一句立刻列舉發胖、腰酸背痛、心臟問題等健康影響，因此空格要接hurts your health(傷害健康)才能呼應後文，符合選項B。costs you money(花錢)、makes traffic terrible(讓交通更糟)、kills the planet slowly(慢慢摧毀地球)都與後文描述的健康問題無關。掌握「not only…but also…」前後語意要呼應一致的原則。

stem: People in the city of Munich have spoken their mind: they do not want to host the Winter Olympics in 2022. To the cities that fight for this chance, ____.
options: this sounds like a good idea
this is perhaps a smart answer
this is old news they have heard
explain_zh: 慕尼黑人民拒絕主辦冬奧，對積極爭取主辦權的城市來說是意料之外的消息，因此答案是this is surely a surprise，符合選項A。此段接著解釋奧運通常能帶來工作機會與觀光收入，可知拒辦是「令人驚訝」的決定，並非「聽起來不錯」(B)或「早已耳聞的舊聞」(D)。掌握「So why did people in Munich say no?」的疑問語氣可幫助判斷空格語意。
passage:
People in the city of Munich have spoken their mind: they do not want to host the Winter Olympics in 2022. To the cities that fight for this chance, ____. The Olympics usually do a lot of good to the host city. The Games bring in jobs, visitors, and, most important of all, money. So why did people in Munich say no?
The Olympics ____ for people in Munich. For them, the world's biggest sports festival could invite serious trouble. There would be a lot of building work before the Games, and during the Games, too much traffic and too many visitors. Life would become terrible and nature would be hurt. And ____: Munich hosted the 1972 Summer Olympics, and its neighbor, the mountain town Garmisch-Partenkirchen, hosted the 1936 Winter Olympics.
Still, the heavy price Munich paid does not worry the cities that are in the race to get the 2022 Winter Olympics. ____, they are happy that Munich said no to the Olympics—their chances of getting the Games have become higher.

stem: The Olympics ____ for people in Munich. For them, the world's biggest sports festival could invite serious trouble.
explain_zh: 對慕尼黑居民而言，奧運不是帶來好處，反而可能帶來嚴重麻煩(施工、交通壅塞、環境破壞)，因此用are a different story(是另一回事、另當別論)最貼切，符合選項B。had given hopes(曾帶來希望)、bring a bright future(帶來光明前景)、have been a great plan(是很棒的計畫)語氣都偏正面，與後文描述的「serious trouble」矛盾。從後文的負面敘述可反推空格應選轉折語氣的選項。

options: this will not go away; it will stay
they are not just saying it; they are going to do it
they do not speak for others; they only speak for themselves
this is not a guess; it is a lesson they learned from hard experience
explain_zh: 後面舉出慕尼黑與鄰近城鎮過去實際主辦奧運的例子作為證據，顯示這不是憑空猜測，而是親身經歷得來的教訓，符合選項D。this will not go away(不會消失)、they are not just saying it(他們不只是說說而已)、they only speak for themselves(他們只代表自己)，語意都無法自然銜接「舉出過去真實經驗佐證」的用意。看到後面接著具體歷史事件當例子，就是「真實經驗、不是臆測」的訊號。
